artists.biography:
Screaming Trees was an American rock band formed in Ellensburg, Washington in 1985 by vocalist Mark Lanegan, guitarist Gary Lee Conner, bass player Van Conner and drummer Mark Pickerel. Pickerel had been replaced by Barrett Martin by the time the band reached its most successful period. Although widely associated with grunge, the band's sound incorporated hard rock and psychedelic elements. Since its formation, Screaming Trees released seven studio albums, five EPs and three compilations.

Screaming Trees is known as one of the "Godfathers of Grunge" along with the Melvins, U-Men, Skin Yard, Soundgarden, Green River, Cosmic Psychos and Malfunkshun. Screaming Trees rose to fame as part of the grunge movement of the early 1990s, along with bands such as Alice in Chains, Stone Temple Pilots, Pearl Jam, Nirvana and Soundgarden and was one of the most successful underground music acts of the 1990s. The band achieved one top ten single on the Modern Rock Tracks charts. Screaming Trees were plagued by extended inactivity due to their problems with making a follow up to Dust. This led to their official breakup in 2000.

perplexity.description:
Uncle Anesthesia is the fifth studio album by American rock band Screaming Trees, released on January 29, 1991, through Epic Records. Marking the band's major-label debut, the album blends psychedelic rock, grunge, and alternative rock, showcasing the group's signature heavy guitar textures, atmospheric production, and Mark Lanegan's distinctive, gravelly vocals. The record features a dynamic range of songwriting, from brooding, blues-tinged tracks to more aggressive, riff-driven numbers, reflecting the band's evolution from their earlier, more experimental sound toward a more polished and accessible style.

In the context of Screaming Trees' discography, Uncle Anesthesia represents a pivotal transition, bridging their underground roots with broader mainstream exposure. It incorporates two tracks from their 1990 EP Something About Today, further solidifying their new direction. While the album did not achieve major commercial success upon release, it received positive critical attention for its sonic depth and the band's growing maturity. Critics praised its atmospheric production and Lanegan's emotive delivery, positioning Uncle Anesthesia as a key release in the early 1990s alternative rock landscape.
